title: Maryville Alcoa Animal Rescue Center Dog of the Week: Freya - NewsBreak
text:
By Shanon Adame ,
41 minutes ago
What happens when you mix a Tasmanian devil with a golden retriever, and sprinkle in extra cuddles? You get Freya! The cutest little rascal this side of East Tennessee.
Freya used to star in Looney Tunes cartoons, alongside viewer favorites like Wile E. Coyote and Droopy. On screen, she’d chase her tail so fast she’d end up a tiny tornado, blasting off into another dimension!
Sometimes she’d sit with boxes and boxes of Milkbones and eat treats until she had to slide across the floor rather than walk.
In the cartoons, whenever she saw people, her eyes turned into big hearts, and little cupids flew around her head. She’d dash right up and give them a big puppy kiss.
But Freya’s favorite gag was activating turbo mode, where flames shot out of her tail, and she ran in loops across the screen, her pink bubblegum tongue trailing behind.
For Freya, life in cartoons was fun, but there were no humans for her to love on, and what Freya wanted more than anything was someone to love. So, one morning, much to the surprise of a family gathered around the TV for Saturday morning cartoons, Freya jumped out of the television.
“Hi! I’m Freya, and I’m fun!” she said with a wag of her tail.
She made her way over to the Maryville Alcoa Animal Rescue Center, where she is waiting for her fur-ever home.
The perfect home for sweet, two-year-old Freya will be one where the treats are delicious, the playtime is fun to the max, and the love is bigger than the biggest cartoon heart.
City employee Sarah De Bruin said Freya is a sweet, high-energy gal who loves, loves, loves…anyone and everything.
Living in cartoons didn’t give Freya too much puppy etiquette, but this eager-to-please girl should be a breeze to train.
At 60 pounds, she is the perfect size for couch cuddles and sweet snuggles.
“I’m ready to love in real life,” Freya said with puppy dog eyes.
For more information on Freya or other adoptable furry friends, call Maryville Alcoa Animal Rescue Center at 865-273-3751.
The center is located at 426 Home Ave., Maryville.
